chunk_findings.detail: The change contains no product-code line at all (the diff is tests-only), so the added test cannot be the fail-first regression test the change's own intent demands ("Write the regression test first and watch it FAIL on the unfixed code"). Check the pre-change revision (`git stash` the test edit and run `uv run pytest -q tests/test_hook_core.py -k pinned_session_start`): the test still passes green, because everything it asserts — that the *default* strategy renders an `(auto …)` marker and that `config --set schedule.parallel fixed` renders `(fixed)` instead — is pre-existing config→string behaviour that existed before this diff, and the test deliberately writes its own pin rather than depending on the edit to `test_the_session_start_alias_and_the_entry_point_print_the_same_brief`. The only genuine detector of B6983363359 is the `a[1] == b[1]` equality check in the sibling test, and that check remains load-dependent by construction (that is exactly why it had to be pinned); the new test's two substring assertions cannot substitute for it, since they constrain neither the value of `N` in the `parallel:` line nor any other host-derived token. Concretely: a later change that keeps the `(fixed)` label but still derives the number (or appends a load/mem figure) from the host leaves the new test green (`"(fixed)" in text and "(auto" not in text` both hold) while the same-brief test flakes again under load — i.e. the bug this change claims to close is not actually locked down. To be a real regression guard the test would have to force the load-dependent path deterministically (e.g. stub the load/memory probe, or run the two briefs under a simulated load change) and assert equality across them.

chunk_findings.detail: The new refusal gate at `ddflow/api/gates.py:626` keys entirely off `scope.needs_ci`, and `needs_ci` is not a fact about the scope — it is a substring test against the human-readable reason: `Scope("full", why, needs_ci="rerun ci" in why)`. Eligibility for "refuse instead of launching the suite" is therefore decided by prose. That the coupling is real and easy to break is demonstrated by this diff itself: four separate messages in `_ci_not_passed_here` (lines ~145, ~148, ~152, ~155) had to be reworded to contain the literal `rerun ci` — before this change they said "this gate runs the whole suite", and the flag would have been `False` for all of them. Concretely, the refusal set is decided by wording, not by condition: the branch at testscope.py:145 ("no ci gate in this item's pipeline runs the whole suite, so this gate runs it") is reached on the same code path, yields `scope.scope == "full"`, and does not contain `rerun ci`, so `needs_ci` stays `False` and `ddflow gate run <id> unit_tests` still starts `pytest tests/ -n 24` from an item gate — the behaviour the stated intent forbids ("never start the full suite from an item gate"). Because the flag and the gate that consumes it are coupled only by a string constant with no test or type expressing the invariant, any rewording of the remaining four messages (or any message assembled such that the phrase is paraphrased, e.g. "run ci again") silently restores bug B9de2a7dc3e: the refusal at gates.py:626 no longer fires and the 13k-test suite is launched unasked again.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/testscope.py:107 (`needs_ci="rerun ci" in why`)

chunk_findings.detail: The diff is still tests-only: no product-code line changed, so the "fix" for B6983363359 is entirely a change to how the tests configure the repo. The change's own intent requires a regression test that *fails on the unfixed revision* ("Write the regression test first and watch it FAIL on the unfixed code; then `ddflow complete … --regression-test <test>`"). The new test cannot satisfy that by construction: `_three_tasks(repo)` immediately issues `run_cli(repo, "config", "--set", "schedule.parallel", "fixed")` before `_brief_around_a_loaded_sample(repo)` is called, so the assertion `a == b and "(fixed)" in a` depends only on the pinned setting, not on any behaviour that the change fixes. Apply the whole diff to the pre-change revision and the test passes; revert it and the test does not exist — there is no input for which it fails first. The author's triage probe (the auto-mode flake not reproducing in 360 runs at `-n16`) shows only that the original flake is not reproducible on that host, which is precisely why it does not answer the requirement: not reproducing a flake is not the same as producing a fail-first test, and the "replacement" test pins the very setting it is supposed to validate. The same masking also removes the auto/load-dependent path from the test that claims to fix the bug: `test_the_session_start_alias_and_the_entry_point_print_the_same_brief` now forces `fixed` before comparing the two briefs, so neither the fixed nor the replaced test exercises the default `(auto …)` rendering the bug is about. The finding therefore still holds, unfixed.

chunk_findings.detail: The new flag is derived from pipeline membership (`needs_ci="ci" in G.pipeline_for(it, cfg)`), but it is attached to *every* non-empty reason returned by `_ci_not_passed_here` — including the reason `"no ci gate in this item's pipeline runs the whole suite, so this gate runs it"`. That reason is not about `ci` being absent from `it`'s pipeline; it is the case where a gate named `ci` *is* in the pipeline but does not itself cover the whole suite (that is precisely why the message is phrased about a ci gate "runs the whole suite", and why this module has to compare the ci gate's coverage with the gate under test at all — otherwise a partial `ci` tree would be used as a whole-suite anchor for the selection). In that configuration `"ci" in G.pipeline_for(it, cfg)` evaluates True, so `gates.py` takes the new refusal branch and returns `scope.why` verbatim: the user sees a refusal whose reason says `"...so this gate runs it"`, plus ineffective advice to rerun `ci`. Rerunning cannot clear it: whether the item's `ci` gate runs the whole suite is a static property of the item/config, so `_ci_not_passed_here` returns the same non-empty reason on every subsequent run, and `ddflow gate run <id> unit_tests` stays refused forever (the `ci` gate itself is not rescued by the `a {what} runs the whole suite` early return either, since it is not a full gate). Only `--force` gets past it. The flag should be set only for the reasons a rerun of `ci` actually clears (the state/tree-evidence reasons), e.g. by setting `needs_ci=True` inside those branches rather than wrapping every non-empty `why`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/testscope.py:107 (with ddflow/api/gates.py:626)

chunk_findings.detail: The assertion `"selected_tests" not in ev` is now vacuously true and no longer checks what it was written to check. In the refusal path `_run_unit_tests` returns the synthesized dict `{"scope_why": ..., "body": body}` (see the helper change at line 95), which by construction never contains a `selected_tests` key, so the clause can never fail regardless of what the gate actually returned. Before this diff the same clause ran against the real `body["evidence"]` returned by the CLI, so it could catch a gate that refused with exit 3 but still reported a selection. Given input "ci gate has no outcome" the test now passes even if the underlying JSON contained `evidence: {"selected_tests": [...]}`, because that payload is stashed under `ev["body"]` and never inspected. If the intent is to prove the item gate does not select tests when ci is stale, the check needs to be applied to `ev["body"]["evidence"]` (asserting it is absent/empty), not to the wrapper dict.
